step1_analysis.description: A single-ended cascode amplifier featuring an NMOS input (XM2), an NMOS cascode device (XM3) to reduce the Miller effect and increase output impedance, an NMOS tail current source (XM4), and a PMOS active load (XM1).

paper_reference.title: An Ultra-Low-Power Receiver Using TransmittedReference and Shifted Limiters for In-Band Interference Resilience

voltage_gain.description: Maximum AC voltage gain from the input to the output node.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm2 * (Rout_cascode || Rout_pmos). With W/L=5u/0.5u and Id~200uA, gm~1mS and Rout~100kOhm. Intrinsic gain can reach 30-40 dB depending on exact bias.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports various gain figures (12dB, 30dB) for different receiver blocks. A cascode stage in 130nm typically yields 20-40dB of intrinsic gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2 * pi * Rout * C_load). Assuming Rout=100kOhm and C_load=10fF, BW ~ 150MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Bandwidth is highly dependent on the load capacitance. With a minimal parasitic load, it can easily exceed the 20MHz IF bandwidth reported in the paper.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the circuit from the 1.8V supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: Power = VDD * I_tail. With Vbias=0.9V on XM4 (W/L=10), I_tail ~ 200uA. Power = 1.8V * 200uA = 360uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Consistent with 'ultra-low-power' receiver design, individual amplifier/mixer branches typically consume sub-mW power.

dc_operating_point.description: DC voltage at the output node (N3).

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the Vsg required by the PMOS load to source the tail current. Typically designed to sit near VDD/2 for maximum swing.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A well-biased amplifier should have its output DC voltage roughly in the middle of the supply range to keep all transistors in saturation.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure AC voltage gain, 3-dB bandwidth, DC power consumption, and transient response. A large inductor is used to diode-connect the PMOS load at DC for robust biasing, while keeping it as a high-impedance current source at AC.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Cascode Amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

XM1 N3 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N2 LABEL_NET_0 N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N3 VDD N2 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N0 LABEL_NET_1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

* Power Supply
VVDD VDD 0 1.8

* Biasing and Inputs
VLABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 dc 0.9 ac 1 sin(0.9 10m 1Meg)

* Robust DC Biasing for PMOS Load (Diode-connected at DC, Current Source at AC)
Lbias N3 N1 1000H
Cac N1 0 100m

* Load Capacitance
CL N3 0 10f

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power
print v(N3)

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 100 1k 10G
let gain_db = vdb(N3)
meas ac max_gain max gain_db
meas ac bw_freq when gain_db=(max_gain-3) fall=1

* 3. Transient Analysis
tran 1n 2u
meas tran vout_pp pp v(N3)
meas tran vout_max max v(N3)
meas tran vout_min min v(N3)

quit
.endc
.end
